title: openai-chat-completions-parity: params/roles/stop/logprobs/formatting + streaming stability
author: Evan Turner
description: Backfills OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity across the compatibility layer and SDKs. This PR implements parameter mapping for OpenAI-style fields (temperature, top_p, n, max_tokens, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty), normalizes role semantics (system/user/assistant and common aliases), adds stop-sequence handling for both streaming and non-streaming code paths, and wires logprobs through the runtime + compatibility layer so consumers can request token-level scores in parity with OpenAI. It also includes structured output improvements to better support tool/function calling and ensures streaming framing matches OpenAI semantics to avoid truncated or duplicated tokens. Motivation: several customers reported subtle differences when switching from OpenAI to Redwood endpoints: role normalization issues, missing logprobs, and incorrect streaming termination with stop sequences. This caused incorrect downstream parsing for tool-calls and downstream eval regressions. Changeset summary: - Parameter mapping and validation layer in redwood-openai-compat - Role aliasing and conversation serializer fixes in redwood/runtime - Stop handling for prefix/KV cache + streaming termination in serving runtime - Logprobs propagation and wire-format serialization for both streaming and batch responses - Structured output hints and function-call metadata to match OpenAI's shape - SDK updates (python/ts) to preserve response compatibility and typings - Streaming encoder/backpressure fixes to address flaky e2e failures Notes on compatibility and performance: legacy OpenAI param synonyms are accepted and mapped; no immediate breaking changes but synonyms will be deprecated after a grace period. Enabling logprobs incurs additional compute and is opt-in; measured ~2% median token-latency increase on p3 for logprobs responses in our perf suite, mitigated by a quantization execution path for supported models. Checklist: - [x] Add param mapping layer and unit tests - [x] Normalize roles across inputs/outputs - [x] Implement stop sequence handling + streaming termination tests - [x] Wire logprobs through runtime + add integration tests - [x] Structured output metadata + tool/function-call compatibility tests - [x] SDK integration tests (python + ts) - [x] Update docs and changelog - [x] Add benchmark/regression checks in CI Related work: Linear ENG-4921 (compat parity), ENG-4989 (streaming stability).
